title: Alhazen guide
intro: Every experiment starts in one of 7 modes. Simulate, test and run share one code path and differ only in trial counts, who supplies the gaze and keys, and where the data goes.

modes.summary: measure what this rig actually does: display, response keys, eye tracker
modes.data: a measurement report, printed and written next to the rig file

modes.summary: look at the stimulus, with no trials and no data
modes.data: nothing: no trials and no data

modes.summary: write the stimulus to movie files, for a demo you can send
modes.data: movie files and a contact sheet in the folder given with --out

modes.summary: the whole session, driven by a simulated subject
modes.data: <data root>-rehearsal, a sibling the analysis never reads as subjects

modes.summary: the whole session with fewer trials, for a person to sit through once
modes.data: <data root>-rehearsal, a sibling the analysis never reads as subjects

modes.summary: one stage of the monkey training ladder, paid on that stage's success
modes.data: <data root>-training/<ladder>/<stage>/, never the experiment's own root

items.title: Phases last whole frames
items.text: A phase of d seconds is on screen for d to the nearest display frame. The frame its time runs out on is drawn by the next phase, so nothing stays up a frame late.

items.title: Events carry the flip's time
items.text: A visual event is stamped with the time of the screen flip that showed it, not the moment the code asked for it; device messages and sync pulses follow that flip.

items.title: Durations in milliseconds or frames
items.text: A Duration is given in ms or in display frames and is resolved once, against the measured refresh rate, when the session is built.

items.title: The refresh rate is measured and checked
items.text: Frame arithmetic uses the measured refresh rate after checking it agrees with the rig file's rate within its tolerance; a disagreement stops the session instead of silently changing every frame-based duration.

items.title: Dropped frames are counted
items.text: Every frame interval is logged. The rig's frame-QA policy decides what a trial with dropped frames does; under recycle_trial it ends as DROPPED_FRAMES and its condition is served again.

items.title: Development rigs never collect real data
items.text: Run and training modes refuse a rig whose file says real_data: false before anything is opened or written. Every other mode may rehearse on it.

items.title: Flags belong to one mode
items.text: --headless is honoured only by simulate, --mouse only by test; any other mode refuses the flag by name rather than ignoring it.

items.title: A failed device aborts the trial
items.text: If a device stops while the measurement is being made, the trial ends as ABORTED with the fault on its row and its condition is served again; during the closing phase the fault is only flagged.

items.title: Measure the rig itself
items.text: Measure mode checks the display, the response keys and the eye tracker through the same code a session uses, and reports what it measured.

items.title: The params file declares the subject
items.text: A human session opens no reward line, whatever the rig has. A monkey session requires a reward block and pays only the outcomes it names. A file that declares neither keeps the behaviour of versions before 2.12.

items.title: Training pays one stage's success
items.text: Training mode runs the stage the operator chooses, pays only that stage's success (and the device-fault reward), refuses a human subject, and never advances a subject by itself: criteria are recommendations.

items.title: Calibrate before trial 1
items.text: With a real tracker the session asks for a calibration before the first trial. Calibrating is the default; reusing the previous calibration is a separate key, offered only when this rig's own record says it fits. Stand-ins (mouse, simulation) are never asked.

items.title: Calibration targets
items.text: Run, test and training can choose what the tracker draws: the standard target, chosen pictures or random pictures, still or pulsating.

items.title: How conditions are served
items.text: A task's paradigm block chooses the scheduler. A trial that did not complete (a fixation break, an abort) is served again rather than counted.

items.title: Session length before launch
items.text: The workspace estimates a session's length from the effective parameters, mode and rig, and says what it cannot know (waits on the subject, adaptive designs).

items.title: Methods travel with the code
items.text: An experiment's methods, parameter reference, timelines and stimulus schematics are written by its authors and versioned with its package. Defaults are checked against the package's params file when it is uploaded.

items.title: Figures explain; they do not measure
items.text: Timelines draw only known durations to scale; phases that wait on the subject or happen only sometimes are marked as such. Schematics show the design in degrees of visual angle, not a measurement of your rig.

items.title: Missing documentation is said plainly
items.text: A package without documentation is shown as undocumented. Read its source and parameter files before running it.
